hints: Look at where each unloading arrow meets the extension axis - plastic means the sample does not return to zero extension.
Compare graphs C and D: both show loops, but only one leaves a residual extension when force returns to zero.
Recall that plastic flow beyond the elastic limit leaves a permanent set, so the unloading line is displaced to the right on the extension axis.
walkthrough: Identify the test for plastic deformation: after the force is removed, extension is not zero, so the unloading curve must hit the extension axis at a positive value.
Check graphs A and B: the arrows go out and return along the same line to the origin, so extension is fully recovered and deformation is elastic.
Check graph C: unloading follows a lower loop showing hysteresis, but it still returns to the origin, so there is no permanent extension.
Check graph D: loading is initially straight then curves, and unloading follows a straight line that meets the extension axis at a positive extension.
That residual extension at zero force is permanent plastic set. This is option D

A.explanation: Loading and unloading follow the same straight line back to zero extension, so deformation is elastic and obeys Hooke's law with no permanent set.

B.explanation: Loading and unloading follow the same curved path back to zero extension, so deformation is non-linear elastic with no permanent extension.

C.explanation: Unloading forms a hysteresis loop but returns to zero extension, as for rubber, so there is energy loss but no plastic permanent extension.

D.explanation: Unloading returns parallel to the initial elastic line but meets the extension axis above zero, leaving a permanent extension characteristic of plastic deformation.
